stories.headline: DeepSeek open-sources DeepInfer, the inference stack behind its production service

key_facts.fact: On Oct 20, 2026, DeepSeek open-sourced DeepInfer, its in-house inference framework that powers DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash at scale, saying it wants to help the community lower compute costs and energy use.
key_facts.excerpt: Introducing DeepInfer, our in-house inference framework, now fully open source! Powering DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash at scale with high throughput and low latency. We're sharing our production stack to help the community lower compute costs, reduce energy use, and make AI more affordable.

key_facts.fact: DeepInfer is released under the Apache 2.0 license and supports NVIDIA SM100 GPUs and Huawei Ascend 950 NPUs.
key_facts.excerpt: License: Apache License 2.0 ... Supported hardware: NVIDIA SM100 GPUs; Huawei Ascend 950 NPUs

key_facts.fact: Features include optimized kernels (FlashMLA, DeepGEMM, DeepEP), MoE expert parallelism, speculative decoding with draft tokens, SWA bounded replay, batch-invariant inference, deterministic sampling and structured outputs.
key_facts.excerpt: Optimized kernels: FlashMLA, DeepGEMM, DeepEP, TileKernels, DeepSelect ... DSpark and confidence-scheduled verification ... SWA bounded replay ... Batch-invariant inference ... Deterministic sampling ... Structured outputs

key_facts.fact: The release omits a KV cache system, prefill/decode disaggregation and load balancing across replicas, so it is not a complete serving stack.
key_facts.excerpt: Required for a complete inference service (not included in this release): A KV cache system; VE/Prefill/Decode disaggregation ...; Load balancing across data-parallel replicas

key_facts.fact: DeepSeek said inference code for its future models will also be published in DeepInfer, and it separately open-sourced deepseek-recipe, its production token encoding/decoding component aligned with the official API.
key_facts.excerpt: Inference code for future DeepSeek models and ongoing optimizations will land here too.

key_facts.fact: Bloomberg framed the release as potentially making DeepSeek's technology cheaper and easier for businesses to run.
key_facts.excerpt: DeepSeek is opening up the software it uses to run its artificial intelligence models at scale, potentially making its technology cheaper and easier for businesses to run.

stories.headline: Inception releases Mercury 3, a diffusion LLM running at 1,000+ tokens per second

key_facts.fact: On Oct 19, 2026, Inception released Mercury 3, which CEO Stefano Ermon called the most intelligent diffusion LLM ever released, claiming it outperforms GPT-6 Luna and Claude Haiku 5.5 on quality while running at over 1,000 tokens per second.
key_facts.excerpt: Today, we're releasing Mercury 3. Mercury 3 is by far our most powerful model and the most intelligent diffusion LLM ever released. It outperforms GPT-6 Luna and Haiku 5.5 on quality while running at 1000+ tok/sec. — Stefano Ermon, October 19, 2026

key_facts.fact: Unlike autoregressive models that generate one token at a time, Mercury 3 generates and refines multiple tokens in parallel; Inception claims it is 4x to 8x faster than Haiku 5.5, GPT-6 Luna and GLM-5.3 Flash while beating them on agentic benchmarks.
key_facts.excerpt: Inception claims that Mercury 3 performs 4x to 8x faster than Haiku 5.5, GPT-6 Luna, and GLM-5.3 Flash while performing better than all of them on agentic benchmarks.

key_facts.fact: On Inception's own benchmark table, Mercury 3 leads GPT-6 Luna and Haiku 5.5 on 8 of 12 tests, including SWE-Bench Atlas (51.08 vs 33.33 and 32.26), but trails Haiku 5.5 on DeepSWE v1 (46.31 vs 51.62).
key_facts.excerpt: Leads 8 of 12 benchmarks vs GPT-6 Luna and Haiku 5.5 (self-reported, medium settings). Best: SWE-Bench Atlas 51.08, about 18 points ahead of both rivals. Worst: DeepSWE v1 46.31, 5.31 points behind Haiku 5.5 (51.62).

key_facts.fact: Mercury 3 has a 1M-token context window and more than 40 times the parameters of Mercury 1; Inception did not disclose the parameter count.
key_facts.excerpt: Size: Parameters not disclosed. Inception says it is more than 40x larger than Mercury 1. Context is 1M tokens.

key_facts.fact: Launch pricing is $0.10 per million input tokens and $0.35 per million output tokens, 50% off the list price of $0.20/$0.70.
key_facts.excerpt: List pricing is $0.20 per 1M input and $0.70 per 1M output tokens. At launch it is 50% off: $0.10 and $0.35.

key_facts.fact: Inception said it used swarms of Mercury 3 agents for recursive self-improvement, which increased the model's overall speed by 16% beyond the upgrades made by its team.
key_facts.excerpt: Inception also reported that it implemented swarms of Mercury 3 agents for recursive self improvement where they increased the overall speed of the model by 16% on top of the upgrades made by the Inception team itself.

key_facts.fact: Mercury 3 is available via the Inception API, OpenRouter, Baseten and Vercel; it is API-only with no open weights.
key_facts.excerpt: Mercury 3 is live on the Inception API Platform, OpenRouter, Baseten and Vercel.

stories.headline: OpenAI says its new models jump in COBOL, Fortran and Visual Basic coding and migration

key_facts.fact: On Oct 19, 2026, OpenAI said its latest models bring stronger capabilities for building and migrating software in low-resource programming languages such as COBOL, Fortran and Visual Basic, which power software that banks, governments and businesses depend on.
key_facts.excerpt: Our latest model advances bring stronger capabilities for building and migrating software in low-resource programming languages such as COBOL, Fortran, and Visual Basic. These languages power software that banks, governments, and businesses depend on.

key_facts.fact: On OpenAI's new MultiLangBench, which asks a model to build a SQLite-compatible database engine in 20 languages, GPT-6 Astra averaged an 87.4% test pass rate, up from 26.8% for GPT-5.6 Sol; COBOL rose from 10.9% to 72.1%.
key_facts.excerpt: It said GPT-6 Astra had an average test pass rate of 87.4 percent across 20 languages, making it a lot of effective than GPT-5.6 Sol that had a 26.8 percent pass rate. COBOL remains the hardest language to crack, with Astra's pass rate being 72 percent.

key_facts.fact: On a COBOL migration test to C++, Java, Kotlin, Python or Rust requiring byte-for-byte output parity, GPT-6.1 Sol scored 86.6% at low reasoning effort versus 5.4% for GPT-5.6 Sol, and 97.9% at higher effort.
key_facts.excerpt: GPT-6.1 Sol scored 86.6% on COBOL migration at low effort. GPT-5.6 Sol scored 5.4% at the same setting, and GPT-6.1 Sol did it at 61% of the API cost. At higher reasoning effort, accuracy reached 97.9%

key_facts.fact: GPT-6 Luna reached 40.3% on MultiLangBench at an estimated $0.77 per sample, about 78% cheaper than GPT-5.6 Sol's $3.48.
key_facts.excerpt: GPT-6 Luna reached 40.3% at an estimated average API cost of $0.77 per sample, compared with $3.48 for GPT-5.6 Sol, about 78% lower.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI cites COBOL as supporting more than 40% of online banking systems and 95% of ATM transactions, and is releasing MultiLangBench on GitHub; it says production migrations still require expert review.
key_facts.excerpt: COBOL supports more than 40% of online banking systems, 80% of in-person credit card transactions and 95% of ATM transactions ... On its new MultiLangBench evaluation, which OpenAI is releasing on GitHub

stories.headline: US DHS orders DeepSeek technology removed from federal civilian IT systems

key_facts.fact: On Oct 19, 2026, DHS made public an order requiring federal civilian agencies to remove DeepSeek technology from their IT systems and barring future purchases of its products and services.
key_facts.excerpt: The Department of Homeland Security has ordered federal civilian agencies to remove artificial-intelligence technology developed by China's DeepSeek from their information technology systems. The order also bars future purchases of DeepSeek's products and services

key_facts.fact: The order, issued under the Federal Acquisition Supply Chain Security Act of 2018, also covers DeepSeek affiliates and third-party products and services built using DeepSeek implementations.
key_facts.excerpt: Pursuant to the authority granted by the Federal Acquisition Supply Chain Security Act of 2018 ... removal of all DeepSeek and DeepSeek affiliate products, and third-party products and services developed using DeepSeek implementations, from civilian agency information technology.

key_facts.fact: The order was originally issued on July 24 and applies to civilian agencies including Treasury, State and Justice, but excludes the Department of Defense; agencies can request exceptions within 60 days.
key_facts.excerpt: The order, originally issued on July 24, applies to federal civilian agencies, including the Treasury, State and Justice departments, but it excludes the Department of Defense.

key_facts.fact: DHS said DeepSeek models present 'multiple threat vectors' and that use 'may result in the transfer of sensitive data to the PRC', and that the models may contain malware or security vulnerabilities.
key_facts.excerpt: DHS said DeepSeek models pose "multiple threat vectors" and raised concerns that use of the product "may result in the transfer of sensitive data to the PRC if used by US government employees or vendors."

key_facts.fact: Several US agencies, including Commerce and the Navy, and states such as New York, Tennessee and Virginia had previously restricted DeepSeek on government devices.
key_facts.excerpt: Previously, several US agencies, including the Department of Commerce and the Navy, have banned the use of DeepSeek on government devices. Multiple states, including New York, Tennessee and Virginia, have taken similar steps.

stories.headline: OpenAI races to close ~$30B round at $1.4T+ valuation before Anthropic's IPO

key_facts.fact: OpenAI is racing to secure investor commitments before Anthropic's expected mid-November IPO, in a round of about $30 billion that could value it at more than $1.4 trillion, Reuters reported on Oct 19, 2026, citing sources.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI is racing to secure investor commitments before rival Anthropic's expected public market debut in mid-November, in an unusually fast fundraising that could value the ChatGPT maker at over $1.4 trillion

key_facts.fact: SoftBank, Abu Dhabi's MGX and other existing backers are in talks to join the round.
key_facts.excerpt: SoftBank Group, Abu Dhabi-based MGX and other existing backers of OpenAI are in talks to join the round of about $30 billion, one of the people said.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI is telling investors it reached $50 billion in annualized revenue after the GPT-6 Astra launch and expects $70 billion by year-end; it has also cut prices on cheaper models and said it could lower prices further.
key_facts.excerpt: saying it had reached $50 billion in annualised revenue and expects that figure to rise to $70 billion by the end of the year ... OpenAI has also cut prices on its cheaper models, which it said has boosted usage, and told investors it could lower the prices of AI models further

key_facts.fact: OpenAI wants to close before Anthropic's financial disclosures invite side-by-side comparisons; it has accused Anthropic of inflating revenue by booking the gross value of cloud-resold contracts, which Anthropic denies.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI is seeking to complete the fundraising before Anthropic's financial disclosures give investors a fuller picture of its business and invite comparisons between the two companies ... It has accused Anthropic of inflating its revenue by counting the full, gross value of contracts sold through third-party cloud providers. Anthropic told Reuters earlier that it follows established accounting practices.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI was last valued at $852 billion in March after a $122 billion round; Anthropic's Q3 revenue rose to $16.8 billion from $11.6 billion in Q2, and some investors have argued for a ~$1.5 trillion IPO valuation instead of the $2 trillion sought.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic informed investors that revenue for the third quarter climbed to $16.8 billion, versus $11.6 billion during the second quarter ... Some current and potential Anthropic investors have pushed for a listing valuation of about $1.5 trillion, not the $2 trillion the company is seeking

stories.headline: AI app startups raise big: Arda $230M at $1.5B, Otter.ai $320M, Town $108M at $1B

key_facts.fact: Arda, the AI manufacturing startup of former OpenAI research chief Bob McGrew, raised $230 million at a $1.5 billion valuation in a round led by Altimeter Capital, Accel and Khosla Ventures, it told CNBC on Oct 20, 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: Bob McGrew's newest company, Arda, has raised $230 million at a $1.5 billion valuation, the company told CNBC in an exclusive interview Tuesday. The round was led by Altimeter Capital, Accel and Khosla Ventures.

key_facts.fact: McGrew described Arda as 'a user interface and an agent that does for manufacturing engineers what Claude or Cursor does for programmers'; its models are already deployed with defense company Anduril.
key_facts.excerpt: "It's a user interface and an agent that does for manufacturing engineers what Claude or Cursor does for programmers," McGrew told CNBC. ... Arda's AI models have already been deployed with military tech company Anduril.

key_facts.fact: In March 2026 Arda was seeking $70 million at a $700 million valuation, so its valuation more than doubled in about seven months.
key_facts.excerpt: In March 2026, the company was seeking $70 million at a $700 million valuation. About seven months later, it has a raise more than three times that target. Its valuation has more than doubled.

key_facts.fact: Meeting note-taker Otter.ai raised $320 million in non-dilutive capital from General Catalyst's Customer Value Fund; it had raised $50 million in total before, and says 40 million people have used its product, up from 25 million last year.
key_facts.excerpt: Otter.ai announced on Tuesday that it has raised $320 million from General Catalyst's Customer Value Fund (CVF), which provides capital to startups without diluting equity ... The company said that 40 million users have used its product to date, up from 25 million last year.

key_facts.fact: Town, an enterprise AI assistant startup founded by former Plaid CTO Jean-Denis Greze, raised a $108 million Series B co-led by Forerunner Ventures and Menlo Ventures at a $1 billion valuation, four months after its public launch.
key_facts.excerpt: Town ... nabbed a unicorn valuation on Monday, announcing a $108 million Series B funding round co-led by Forerunner Ventures and Menlo Ventures. The company launched publicly just four months ago

key_facts.fact: Town gives each employee an AI assistant ('Townie') connected to email, calendar and work systems; Townies can talk to each other, and Town has raised at least $160 million to date.
key_facts.excerpt: giving each employee an AI assistant called a Townie that helps with tasks by connecting to tools such as emails and calendars ... It has raised at least $160 million to date

stories.headline: Safety advocates slam Anthropic's leaked federal AI bill; company says it will revise it

key_facts.fact: A discussion draft of a federal AI bill Anthropic had circulated to lawmakers, published by Politico on Friday Oct 16, drew broad criticism from AI safety advocates as weaker than the bipartisan FRONTIER Act; Transformer published an analysis on Oct 19.
key_facts.excerpt: A leaked discussion draft of a federal AI bill which Anthropic has been circulating to lawmakers, published by Politico on Friday ... has been widely criticized by AI safety advocates, is much weaker than the Obernolte/Trahan FRONTIER Act

key_facts.fact: The draft requires third-party evaluators to assess catastrophic risk but sets no standards or licensing for them, allowing self-certification.
key_facts.excerpt: Like the FRONTIER Act, it requires third-party evaluators to assess AI companies' models and practices for catastrophic risk. Unlike FRONTIER, however, there are no standards or licensing requirements for evaluators, which can self-certify.

key_facts.fact: To block a dangerous model, the Commerce Department would have to petition a federal court, which decides 'without deference' and must weigh the harm a blocking order would cause to the developer.
key_facts.excerpt: If the Commerce Department ... wants to stop one, it must petition a federal court ... The court decides every question "without deference" ... It must also "consider the harm the [blocking] order would cause to the frontier developer, to users, and to the public."

key_facts.fact: The bill would preempt state frontier-AI laws such as California's SB 53 and New York's RAISE Act while carving out child safety laws.
key_facts.excerpt: laws like California's SB 53, New York's RAISE and Illinois' SB 315 that seek to govern "frontier AI" would be preempted, while child safety and other laws are explicitly carved out.

key_facts.fact: On Oct 19, Anthropic's head of federal affairs Anthony Cimino said the text was an early draft, that it does not absolve companies of liability, and that Anthropic wants to work with policymakers to make it 'as strong as it can be'; he had earlier said the preemption language would be adjusted.
key_facts.excerpt: This was our early draft proposal for addressing specific types of catastrophic harm from AI at the federal level. We are not proposing it should be the sole accountability mechanism the government can use. Nor does the bill absolve companies of liability when they inflict harm. We are also interested in working with policymakers to revisit this to ensure it is as strong as it can be.
